summary: One mole of a perfect gas in a cylinder with a piston has pressure P, volume V and temperature T. If its…
alt: Ex NP 8.3: One mole of a perfect gas in a cylinder with a piston has pressure P, volume V and temperature T. If its temperature is increased by 1 K. Find the increase in volume, if initial volume was 100 m³. (Ans: 0.37 m³)

constant P (free piston): V₁ / T₁ = V₂ / T₂

steps.title: Read the question
steps.text: A mole of gas under a free piston is warmed by \( 1 \) K from \( V_1 = 100 \) m³. Find \( \Delta V \). (The initial temperature is not given.)

steps.title: Assumption
steps.text: The book answer matches \( T_1 = 273 \) K, so we take that. (A real mole of gas is far smaller than 100 m³; the question just uses the number.)

steps.title: Charles's law
steps.text: At constant pressure \( V_1/T_1 = V_2/T_2 \), so \( \Delta V = V_1\,\Delta T/T_1 \).

challenges.title: Now you try
challenges.prompt: A gas at 300 K and 60 m³ is warmed by 1 K at constant pressure. Find ΔV (m³).

takeaways: \( \Delta V = V_1\Delta T/T_1 \) at constant pressure (T₁ taken as 273 K).
